I have been farming these 9 mu for forty years, and I know what works on this land. My household has seven mouths to feed, and with some of my family working off-farm, I do not have extra labor to waste. The wheat-maize rotation is the only system I have ever trusted here in Quzhou.

For **winter wheat**, I will sow my 9 mu in early October after rotary tillage. I buy improved wheat seed from the shop every year — saved seed loses vigor, and I cannot afford a bad stand. I will put down compound fertilizer as a basal dressing, and then top-dress with urea at green-up and jointing. All together that comes to about 17 kg of nitrogen per mu. I do not bother with phosphate or potash — they cost too much, and on this land I do not see the benefit. Because I have a well, I will irrigate four times: at green-up, jointing, heading, and grain filling. Wheat cannot suffer drought at those stages. I will spray herbicide once after sowing, and apply insecticide two or three times during the growing season if I see aphids or other pests. I expect about 500 kg per mu if the weather cooperates.

For **summer maize**, I sow right after the wheat harvest in early June. I never till for maize — there is no time between harvest and sowing, and no-tillage saves me labor when my family is busy. I always buy hybrid seed, usually something like Denghai 605. It costs more, but the yield is worth it. I do not apply extra nitrogen to the maize — the leftover fertility from the wheat is enough, and adding more just wastes money. I will irrigate two or three times, mainly at the big-trumpet stage and grain filling. I will spray for weeds once and for insects twice. I expect about 550 kg per mu.

This is the same plan I have followed for years. The inputs are not fancy, but they are what my land and my labor can manage.
